claim: RAUC runs the system pre-install handler before any slot is written and marks the new slot active (r_mark_active, inside the default install handler) before it runs the post-install handler; this order is the same in v1.13 (Debian 13) and current master. A trial marker written by post-install can therefore be lost to a power cut after the slot is already active.

RAUC system handlers receive RAUC_BUNDLE_MOUNT_POINT, RAUC_TARGET_SLOTS and RAUC_SLOT_BOOTNAME_<N>; RAUC_MF_VERSION is documented only for install hooks, so a handler must read the version from the mounted bundle's manifest.

RAUC's GRUB backend treats a slot as good only when it is in ORDER with _OK=1 and _TRY=0, and mark-good writes _OK=1,_TRY=0; combined with Home Assistant OS's GRUB script (try while TRY<3, increment every boot) this gives exactly 3 boot attempts per unconfirmed slot. Observed in the lab: A_TRY went 1,2,3 then GRUB chose the other slot.

By default k3s writes outside its --data-dir: the admin kubeconfig to /etc/rancher/k3s/k3s.yaml and runtime state under /var/lib/kubelet, /var/lib/cni, /var/log and /etc/rancher (k3s remaps exactly these for rootless mode; the kubelet root moves under the data dir only when rootless). On a read-only A/B root, k3s v1.37.2+k3s1 exited with 'mkdir /etc/rancher/k3s: read-only file system' until these paths were bind-mounted from /data and --write-kubeconfig pointed to /run.
Debian 13 ships RAUC 1.13-3+deb13u1 and trixie-backports had no newer RAUC on 2026-11-11; Debian's busybox 1:1.37.0-6+b9 package has no httpd applet.

claim: Lab (Debian 13 x86_64, RAUC 1.13, k3s v1.37.2+k3s1, QEMU TCG): a good update was committed only after the fresh-signal gate passed 3 times in a row (81 s after the trial boot's gate started); a user app stuck in ErrImagePull did not block the commit.

Lab: an update whose k3s exits at start (unknown flag) and an update whose kubelet never runs (--disable-agent) were both rejected at the 300 s gate deadline, marked bad and rolled back to the previous slot with no human input; the previous slot then passed the fresh check.

Lab: the stale-Ready trap reproduces on RAUC: with k3s state on the shared data partition, a gate that checks only API /readyz, node Ready and CoreDNS availability passed 3 consecutive checks (36-64 s after the gate started; commit after 66 s and 63 s in two runs) and committed an update whose kubelet never ran.

Lab: with 3 boot tries, a kernel-panicking update and an update that hangs after arming the watchdog (QEMU i6300esb, -action watchdog=reset) were each booted exactly 3 times and then GRUB returned to the previous slot; the gate then marked the failed slot bad so it was not tried again.

Lab: a power cut (QEMU SIGKILL) while RAUC copied the image left the box on the previous slot; the pre-install trial marker was cleared and the target marked bad by the gate, and a reinstall committed. A power cut during the first trial boot, before commit, did not abandon the good update: GRUB retried the new slot (TRY=2) and the gate committed it.
